Exercise A – Complete using the correct form of the words in the box
Topic vocabulary in contrast. Use the correct word from each pair to complete the sentences.
  • 1. John Sanders, MP, any involvement in the scandal when asked about it yesterday. (deny / refuse)
    ✓ denied (deny = say it's not true; refuse = say you won't do something)
  • 2. The politician to say more when questioned by reporters this morning. (deny / refuse)
    ✓ refused (refuse + to-infinitive = decline to do something)
  • 3. Johnny Depp rarely invitations to do interviews. (agree / accept)
    ✓ accepts (accept an invitation = agree to receive/attend)
  • 4. Johnny Depp to appear at a press conference to promote his latest film. (agree / accept)
    ✓ agreed (agree + to-infinitive = consent to do something)
  • 5. Did you see the newspaper this morning? (heading / headline)
    ✓ headline (the title of a newspaper story)
  • 6. If you give every paragraph of your report a , it'll be easier to read. (heading / headline)
    ✓ heading (a title for a section of text)
  • 7. Living Today has got a special this month on healthy diets. There are interviews with nutritionists, menus, recipes, and loads of other things too. (feature / article)
    ✓ feature (a special in-depth piece on a topic)
  • 8. There's an interesting in the paper about the Constitution of the European Union. (feature / article)
    ✓ article (a piece of writing in a newspaper/magazine)
  • 9. I generally trust what I hear on the news, but rarely believe anything I read in the . (press / media)
    ✓ press (refers specifically to newspapers/print journalism)
  • 10. The involve print journalism, TV, radio and even electronic forms of communication such as the Internet. (press / media)
    ✓ media (all forms of mass communication)
  • 11. We interrupt this programme to bring you an urgent . (bulletin / newsflash)
    ✓ newsflash (a brief, urgent breaking news announcement)
  • 12. And we'll be back with our regular at seven o'clock. (bulletin / newsflash)
    ✓ bulletin (a regular scheduled news programme)
Exercise B – Circle the correct word or phrase
Choose the correct word in bold.
  • 1. It's a great computer once you get the hang of it.
    ✓ programme (British English for a TV/radio show or schedule)
  • 2. I hate newspapers; they're just full of gossip, scandal and lies!
    ✓ broadsheet (quality newspapers; tabloids are the gossipy ones)
  • 3. As a for a local paper, you don't have to interview people or attend events. You just have to express your opinions about the issues of the day.
    ✓ columnist (writes opinion pieces; a journalist reports news)
  • 4. There's a great show on BBC1 tonight. Contestants have to race through a supermarket as quickly as they can, filling up their trolleys as they go.
    ✓ quiz (a competition show with questions/tasks)
  • 5. On some TV channels, tells you what the next programme is going to be.
    ✓ an announcer (introduces programmes; a commentator describes events)
  • 6. Join us at half past nine for a live of the State Opening of Parliament.
    ✓ broadcast (a live transmission; channel = TV station)
Exercise C – Write one word in each gap
Phrasal verbs. Write the correct particle/preposition to complete each phrasal verb.
  • 1. Please do not over your examination papers until you are instructed to do so.
    ✓ turn (turn over = flip/start)
  • 2. I had to in so many forms. It took me hours!

    ✓ put (put forward = propose/suggest)
  • 4. There was a guy in the street out free tickets to that new quiz show.
    ✓ handing (handing out = distributing)
  • 5. He out that he'd worked in children's TV, but in fact he's never been near a TV studio!

  • 6. Could you up her number in the phone book?
    ✓ look (look up = search for information)
  • 7. She out as one of the finest contemporary British novelists around at the moment.
    ✓ stands (stands out = is notably exceptional)
Exercise D – Sentence transformation
Complete each second sentence using the word given so that it has a similar meaning to the first. Write between two and five words.
  • 1.
    Her latest bestseller was published last month. OUT
    Her latest bestseller last month.
    ✓ came out (come out = be published)
  • 2.
    That story's not true, is it? UP
    You , didn't you?
    ✓ made that story up / made up that story (make up = invent)
  • 3.
    The programme starts at half past six. ON
    The programme at half past six.
    ✓ comes on / goes on (come on / go on = begin broadcasting)
  • 4.
    The documentary didn't really explore why the rainforests are being cut down. INTO
    The documentary didn't really why the rainforests are being cut down.
    ✓ go into / look into (go into / look into = explore in depth)
  • 5.
    I had a quick look at the magazine in the dentist's waiting room. THROUGH
    I the magazine in the dentist's waiting room.
    ✓ flicked through / flipped through (look quickly through pages)
  • 6.
    I don't think we need to mention that now. UP
    I don't think we need to now.
    ✓ bring that up / bring it up (bring up = mention a topic)
  • 7.
    Your lies don't fool me! THROUGH
    I can your lies!
    ✓ see through (see through = not be deceived by)
Exercise E – Choose the correct answer
Phrases and collocations. Choose the best option A, B, C or D.
  • 1. It's not always easy to ………… the difference between fact and opinion.
    ✓ D tell (tell the difference = distinguish)
  • 2. The debate will ………… place tonight.
    ✓ C take (take place = happen)
  • 3. In my …………, freedom of the press must be maintained.
    ✓ B view (in my view = in my opinion)
  • 4. Media mogul Ronald Morduck has ………… control of another tabloid.
    ✓ D taken (take control of = gain control)
  • 5. They ………… a description of the robber on CrimeTime and it sounded like you!
    ✓ D gave (give a description = provide a description)
  • 6. J.K. Rowling has ………… an enormous influence on children's literature.
    ✓ B given (have a given influence → has given an enormous influence)
  • 7. I could spend hours ………… the Internet!
    ✓ A surfing (surfing the Internet = browsing online)
  • 8. They said ………… the news that the price of petrol is going up again.
    ✓ C on (on the news = broadcast on news)
  • 9. The issue ………… question is more complex than you think.
    ✓ C in (in question = being discussed)
  • 10. Watch ………… for words like 'so-called' in articles as they express the writer's bias.
    ✓ D out (watch out for = be alert to)
Exercise F – Correct the word in bold
Each sentence contains an incorrect word (preposition). Write the correct word in the box.
  • 1. He's been described by several critics for our greatest living poet.
    ✓ as (described as = identified as)
  • 2. I think you've confused tabloids by broadsheets.
    ✓ with (confuse X with Y)
  • 3. Do you believe about telepathy?
    ✓ in (believe in = think something exists/is true)
  • 4. There's no point of trying to get an interview with him. He never does interviews!
    ✓ in (there's no point in doing something)
  • 5. According from this report, scientists have discovered a new planet.
    ✓ to (according to = based on what is stated by)
  • 6. The facts in this article don't correspond about my own experience at all.
    ✓ with (correspond with = match/agree with)
Exercise G – Write the missing words in the passage
Water has damaged part of this text. Decide what each missing word was and write it in the numbered space.
The Announcement

The editor sent an e-mail (1) every journalist on the news desk announcing (2) there would be an emergency editorial meeting at one o'clock. I had heard (3) the problems the paper was facing and I heard (4) one of my colleagues that the paper might be going to close. Whatever it was, it was likely (5) be bad news.

At the meeting, the editor told us (6) to tell anyone else yet, but the paper had been taken over by Ronald Morduck. He said he had only been informed (7) the decision that morning. We were all so surprised (8) the news that nobody knew what to say. I made a comment (9) a colleague that it was time to start looking for a new job. The editor heard this, and finally managed to persuade us not (10) quit until we had seen what changes would be made.

✓ (1) to  (2) that  (3) about  (4) from  (5) to  (6) not  (7) of  (8) by  (9) to  (10) to

Exercise I – Complete the text by changing the form of the word in capitals
Change the form of the word in capitals to fit the context.
Politics on TV

I love watching (1) DISCUSS programmes, and I love politics, so you'd think I'd enjoy watching (2) POLITICS being interviewed on TV. But I don't. All too often, (3) JOURNAL ask them the most (4) RIDICULE questions, and, when they do get an interesting question, I sit there watching in (5) BELIEVE as some of the most (6) POWER people in the country give totally (7) CONVINCE responses.

It's as if they don't care whether their reply is (8) BELIEVE or not. Often, they're very poor (9) COMMUNICATE, and they're frequently even more (10) INFORM about key issues than I am. I don't expect them to be particularly (11) HUMOUR – they are serious people, after all – but at least they could say something interesting occasionally. It makes me want to stand for election myself!
